title: Energy Markets are on the Verge of a Disaster!
summary: Financial commentary arguing the Hormuz blockade is a lasting physical supply shock that markets underprice, with inflation feeding through fuel, fertilizer and shipping.

assertions.quote: look at the rising price of gasoline, and simply walk away from the conflict
energy executives are refusing to significantly increase production, pointing to the absolute chaos of the current market

verdicts.note: Dallas Fed surveys show executives prioritising capital discipline; drilling responds to sustained, not volatile, prices.

assertions.quote: The increased costs of fertilizer, diesel, and rerouted shipping have already been baked into the supply chain.

verdicts.note: Energy and freight costs feed into food and goods prices over several months, as seen after the 2022 oil and fertilizer spike.

assertions.quote: Since the 1970s, the oil intensity of the global economy has declined by more than 70%.

verdicts.note: Oil use per unit of real GDP has fallen by well over half since 1973, so the same price shock has a smaller macro effect.

assertions.quote: Both the United States and the United Kingdom saw inflation accelerate to 3.3% in March.

verdicts.note: Energy is a large direct component of CPI, and the March 2026 jump followed the Hormuz closure.

Headline CPI rose from 2.4% in February 2026 to 4.2% in May as the energy index went from +0.5% to +23.5% year over year and core stayed at 2.5-2.8%, so an energy shock did push headline inflation higher in spring 2026; the series do not themselves identify the Iran conflict as the cause.

Regular gasoline went from 2.908 in Feb 2026 to 3.638, 4.103 and 4.479 in Mar-May (+54%), a rise in a direct CPI component large enough to lift headline inflation mechanically; the CPI effect itself is not in this file, so confidence stays moderate.

assertions.quote: the windfall at the wellhead doesn't necessarily reach the kitchen table

verdicts.note: Since the shale boom the net GDP effect of oil shocks on the US is close to neutral, with producer gains roughly offsetting consumer losses, but the burden falls on households while gains accrue to a few states and firms.

assertions.quote: The problem is that you can't yell at inflation until it goes away.

verdicts.note: Retail margins are a small, slow-moving part of the pump price, which tracks wholesale gasoline and crude.

assertions.quote: You can't fix a 20% drop in global hydrocarbon supply with wind turbines in the short term

verdicts.note: Oil is a few percent of power generation in rich countries; its demand is in transport and petrochemicals, which electricity displaces only slowly through EVs.

assertions.quote: the market might not return to equilibrium until 2030 due to this permanent loss of supply

verdicts.note: Prediction; past Gulf disruptions saw prices normalise within a year or two, but this one has no precedent in scale.
